arguments.summary: A critical firewall integrity alert was triggered by suspicious activity originating from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42), a high-criticality finance department endpoint. Investigation confirmed malicious activity including Cobalt Strike beaconing (T1071.001), lateral movement via SMB, and execution of encoded PowerShell from Outlook (T1566.001). The host was compromised via a phishing vector, leading to credential misuse and attempted internal reconnaissance. Despite containment attempts, administrative actions were denied due to policy and targeting issues. No immediate compromise of destination host (10.0.1.1) was found.

timeline.description: Initial outbound HTTPS connection to known-bad IP 198.51.100.23 from WS-FIN-042.
Suspicious rundll32.exe execution from Temp directory on WS-FIN-042.
IDS alert triggered: 'ET TROJAN Cobalt Strike Beacon C2 Activity' from WS-FIN-042.
Failed Kerberos TGT request from WS-FIN-042, indicating possible credential misuse or brute-force attempt.
Successful SMB access from WS-FIN-042 to internal file server (10.0.5.50), indicating lateral movement.
Firewall integrity alert generated for traffic between 10.0.5.14 and 10.0.1.1. Investigation reveals source IP misattribution; true source is 10.0.5.42.
EDR and SIEM correlation confirms malicious PowerShell and DLL loading patterns on WS-FIN-042.
Containment actions (firewall block, EPP quarantine) attempted but denied due to policy misalignment and targeting errors.
